title: Shopping Cart
statement: Build a shopping cart. Each line has a minus and a plus button that change its quantity, and the running item count and subtotal below must always agree with what is on screen. Dropping a quantity to zero removes that line, and an empty cart says so instead of showing a total.

app.js

rubric: The summary is derived from the quantity state on every change, not incremented separately — the two can never drift apart.
A quantity reaching zero removes the line from the list rather than showing a zero row.
An empty cart shows the empty message and hides the summary.
Rows are rebuilt from state rather than patched in place by index, so handlers cannot end up on the wrong item.
Money is formatted to two decimal places rather than shown as a raw float.
curveballs: Actually, add a clear-cart button that empties the whole thing in one click.
Cap each line at a quantity of five and grey out the plus button there.
Show the most expensive line in bold.
